item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-dcb4ee31edbcc325","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The publisher described López Obrador as Mexico’s newly elected president, founder and leader of MORENA, and presented his program as a break with neoliberal policy, corruption, violence, and deference to US interests. This is primarily a contemporaneous description of his stated program and political identity, not independent evidence of implementation or outcomes.","question_ids":["4B.1","5B.1","7B.8","8B.1"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Pre-2023 program and background; useful for stated goals but not direct evidence of 2023 conduct.","ruler_attribution":"The book presents López Obrador’s own political program, but the supplied extract is publisher/editorial description rather than a direct quotation of a formal 2023 act.","limitations":["No 2023 implementation, budget, outcome, or independent verification is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d877b5a781b78609","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that López Obrador’s government presided over democratic backsliding that undermined judicial independence, transparency, and the rule of law, while 13 million people were lifted out of poverty during his government.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.6","4B.10","5B.8","5B.10","6B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Retrospective 2018-2024 assessment; includes the 2023 period but is not confined to it.","ruler_attribution":"HRW attributes the democratic-backsliding assessment to López Obrador’s government and the poverty change to his government’s period.","limitations":["The extract does not isolate 2023 causal contributions or specify the poverty methodology beyond the reported total."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2924593e6b03411a","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In 2023, Mexico’s homicide rate fell from 25.9 per 100,000 in 2022 to 24.9, but remained extremely high; reported disappearances increased. HRW also reported that organized crime accounted for an estimated two-thirds of homicides and that about 70 percent of firearms used in crimes were smuggled from the United States.","question_ids":["2B.8","2B.10","3B.6","3B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023 outcomes, with 2022 comparison and contextual estimates.","ruler_attribution":"The homicide-rate change is based on official figures; organized-crime and firearm estimates are attributed to security analysts and authorities.","limitations":["The extract does not establish that López Obrador’s policies caused the homicide decline or disappearance increase."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2924593e6b03411a","start_unit":4,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"López Obrador proposed and Congress approved a constitutional judicial reform requiring judges, including Supreme Court and Electoral Tribunal justices, to leave office and be replaced by popular elections, while creating a disciplinary tribunal with broad sanctioning powers. UN and Inter-American experts warned that the reform would weaken judicial independence and fair-trial rights. The justice system resolved only 16 percent of criminal investigations in 2022, and torture, arbitrary detention, and prolonged pretrial detention remained widespread.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9","4B.4","4B.10","7B.2","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The reform was approved in September 2024, outside the target year; the justice-system performance and documented abuses provide 2023-period context.","ruler_attribution":"HRW identifies the reform as proposed by López Obrador and reports the justice-system conditions under his administration.","limitations":["The constitutional reform itself is not a 2023 event and should not be treated as a 2023 outcome."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2924593e6b03411a","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Under López Obrador, the government closed the National Human Identification Center and dismissed staff; authorities were slow to implement the 2017 Disappearances Law and failed to investigate many reports. López Obrador repeatedly claimed that the official number of missing people had been exaggerated to harm him politically. Poverty fell from 41.9 percent in 2018 to 36.3 percent in 2022, but extreme poverty was unchanged and the number without health-care access more than doubled.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","5B.7","5B.8","5B.10","6B.2","6B.5","6B.10","7B.1","7B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Includes direct 2023-period institutional and outcome evidence plus 2018-2022 welfare comparisons.","ruler_attribution":"HRW attributes the center closure, implementation failures, and public claims to the López Obrador government or López Obrador.","limitations":["The poverty figures end in 2022 and do not independently establish 2023 change."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2924593e6b03411a","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"During López Obrador’s administration, more than 100 civilian government tasks were transferred to the military; the military often refused transparency requests, and executive orders sought to exempt megaprojects from transparency requirements. Pegasus spyware was reportedly used unlawfully against human rights defenders, journalists, opposition politicians, and senior officials. From December 2018 through March 2024, Article 19 registered 3,408 attacks or threats against journalists, 46 journalists killed, and four disappeared; in 2023, 14 human rights defenders and 18 environmental or land defenders were killed.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10","7B.6","7B.7","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Contains direct 2023 defender-killing data and retrospective 2018-2024 institutional and press-freedom evidence.","ruler_attribution":"HRW attributes the transfers and executive orders to López Obrador and reports surveillance during his administration.","limitations":["Some attack and killing totals span years and do not isolate López Obrador’s personal authorization or knowledge."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2924593e6b03411a","start_unit":9,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"López Obrador’s government expanded military roles and civilian deployment despite limited civilian oversight; soldiers were implicated in torture, arbitrary detention, extrajudicial killings, and disappearances, which civilian authorities rarely investigated effectively. In 2023, Mexico expanded abortion access in some jurisdictions, while legal and practical barriers remained; disability-rights reforms recognized full legal capacity and accessible shelters.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly includes 2023 events and policies, alongside administration-wide military evidence.","ruler_attribution":"HRW attributes military deployment policy to López Obrador’s government; the reforms are attributed to Congress and courts.","limitations":["The extract does not quantify implementation of the disability or abortion reforms in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2924593e6b03411a","start_unit":11,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"López Obrador pursued fossil-fuel investment as a route to energy self-sufficiency; Mexico’s emissions target allowed higher emissions than its earlier Paris commitment, and the Climate Action Tracker rated the plan critically insufficient for the 1.5°C goal.","question_ids":["1B.9","1B.10","5B.1","5B.6","5B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Administration policy and targets relevant to the 2023 period, with some decisions originating before 2023.","ruler_attribution":"HRW attributes the fossil-fuel policy to the López Obrador administration.","limitations":["The source does not provide 2023 emissions outcomes or a full alternative-policy counterfactual."]},{"source_id":"SRC-79006aec939b909e","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"For events of 2023, HRW reported that López Obrador made little progress on extreme criminal violence, migrant abuses, gender-based violence, attacks on journalists and defenders, torture, disappearances, and extrajudicial killings. Poverty fell from 41.9 percent in 2018 to 36.3 percent in 2022, while extreme poverty was unchanged and lack of health-care access more than doubled.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.10","5B.8","5B.10","6B.2","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report is explicitly about events of 2023 but includes welfare comparisons ending in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"HRW attributes the policy record and progress assessment to López Obrador’s presidency.","limitations":["The extract does not provide a complete 2023 welfare outcome series."]},{"source_id":"SRC-79006aec939b909e","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In 2023, the justice system resolved just over 1 percent of all crimes committed in 2022; torture was widely practiced; arbitrary detention remained widespread; mandatory pretrial detention and arraigo violated human-rights standards. A July 2023 appellate ruling allowed some challenges to mandatory detention, but military and navy detentions were often not recorded in the National Detention Registry.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to 2023, with some underlying statistics from 2021-2022 and a 2023 judicial correction.","ruler_attribution":"The conditions occurred under López Obrador’s administration; the appellate correction was judicial.","limitations":["The statistics are not all measured in calendar year 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-79006aec939b909e","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"As of August 2023, more than 266,000 soldiers, marines, and National Guard members were deployed domestically. Government data recorded 5,488 civilians killed by the army from 2007 through July 2023, rarely independently investigated. The military obstructed Ayotzinapa and Cold War-abuse investigations, and López Obrador’s government was accused of attempting to reduce or relabel the missing-person registry after the total surpassed 110,000.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.3","8B.5","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly includes 2023 deployment, killings, investigation, and registry events.","ruler_attribution":"HRW attributes military reliance to López Obrador and reports allegations concerning his government’s handling of the registry.","limitations":["The source does not prove López Obrador personally ordered killings, obstruction, or data manipulation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-79006aec939b909e","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"In 2023, eight journalists were killed by September and authorities continued to investigate journalist crimes inadequately; the protection mechanism lacked staff and funding, and protected journalists and defenders were killed. López Obrador intensified migration enforcement, deploying more than 31,000 soldiers; 40 migrants died in the Ciudad Juárez detention-center fire, while the asylum system expanded but remained severely overstretched.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","6B.2","6B.6","6B.10","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023 events and administration policies.","ruler_attribution":"HRW attributes migration-enforcement policy to López Obrador and reports protection-system shortcomings under his administration.","limitations":["The extract does not establish the president’s personal role in individual killings or the detention-center fire."]},{"source_id":"SRC-79006aec939b909e","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"In 2023, same-sex marriage was available nationwide; 21 states allowed simplified legal gender-marker changes; Congress approved disability-rights reforms and Mexico ratified the Inter-American Convention on Older Persons. At the same time, barriers to abortion, disability inclusion, and protection from gender violence persisted.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","5B.8","6B.3","6B.8","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023 legal and policy developments.","ruler_attribution":"The reforms were enacted by Congress, courts, or treaty processes during López Obrador’s presidency; the extract does not establish his personal authorship.","limitations":["Legal enactment is not proof of uniform implementation or equal incidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-79006aec939b909e","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Mexico supported several UN Human Rights Council accountability initiatives in 2023 and led thematic resolutions on migrants, the death penalty, and disability rights, but did not support continued scrutiny of Russia’s human-rights abuses.","question_ids":["1B.4","2B.6","2B.7","2B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers Mexico’s international positions in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The actions are state positions during López Obrador’s presidency; the extract does not specify his personal direction.","limitations":["No evidence is provided on López Obrador’s individual decision process or domestic implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f6cca9e56ae405a6","start_unit":16,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"López Obrador promised in 2018 to determine the truth about the 43 Ayotzinapa students, but by 2023 their whereabouts remained unknown. Families and international investigators reported that the army withheld key evidence, and the independent experts left in July 2023, saying military obstruction and false denials prevented continued investigation.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.1","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers the 2023 investigation and López Obrador’s unfulfilled 2018 commitment.","ruler_attribution":"HRW reports the president’s promise and attributes failure to force military cooperation to his administration; allegations about concealment are attributed to families and investigators.","limitations":["The source is HRW commentary and includes testimony and allegations; it does not establish a final judicial finding of López Obrador’s personal intent."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f6cca9e56ae405a6","start_unit":21,"end_unit":23,"fact_summary":"López Obrador initially created a truth commission, appointed a respected special prosecutor, invited independent experts, and ordered government cooperation on Ayotzinapa. HRW then reported that he failed to compel the military to release evidence, defended the military as fundamental, and allowed the investigation to stall while the military expanded into hundreds of civilian tasks.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","4B.4","5B.6","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the administration’s 2023 conduct, with preceding institutional decisions for context.","ruler_attribution":"HRW attributes the initial investigative design and subsequent failure to compel military cooperation to López Obrador.","limitations":["HRW’s characterization of motives and willingness is evaluative; the supplied extract does not provide a court finding of intent."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aaac1faa31a1f734","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Mexico remained an electoral democracy with routine alternation in power, but severe rule-of-law deficits, organized-crime violence, official corruption, human-rights abuses, and impunity limited political rights and civil liberties. López Obrador won the 2018 election with 53 percent and could not be reelected under the six-year constitutional term.","question_ids":["3B.10","4B.1","4B.8","4B.10","7B.10","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report assesses 2022 and the political system entering the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the electoral and institutional facts to Mexico’s constitutional and political system.","limitations":["The report is not a 2023 year-end assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aaac1faa31a1f734","start_unit":5,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Freedom House reported that Mexico’s electoral institutions generally administered free and fair elections, but faced attacks and proposed reforms that could weaken their independence. Opposition parties remained competitive and power alternation was realistic, while organized crime and military politicization constrained political choice. Indigenous and Afro-Mexican groups remained underrepresented, although gender quotas produced near parity in Congress.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.7","4B.8","4B.10","8B.2","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Primarily 2021-2022 evidence used as context for 2023 political institutions.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes proposed electoral changes and military-task expansion to López Obrador’s administration; institutional outcomes involve Congress, INE, TEPJF, and courts.","limitations":["Most specific electoral events predate 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aaac1faa31a1f734","start_unit":7,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Anti-corruption enforcement under López Obrador was described as politicized and generally ineffective: opponents were publicly targeted, while investigations involving allies and favored institutions were rare or perfunctory. Transparency was weakened by military opacity, infrastructure exemptions, blocked appointments to the transparency agency, and López Obrador’s repeated attacks on the press; attacks against media workers increased substantially.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","5B.5","5B.7","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Primarily 2021-2022 evidence, relevant to the institutional trajectory entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the political anti-corruption strategy, press attacks, and transparency actions to López Obrador and his administration.","limitations":["The extract does not provide a 2023-specific enforcement dataset."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aaac1faa31a1f734","start_unit":10,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Mexico guaranteed formal assembly and NGO freedoms, but police used excessive force and arbitrary detention against protests; Pegasus surveillance concerns persisted; the government’s protection mechanism was underfunded. The judiciary suffered delays, corruption, weak prosecutorial autonomy, preventive detention, and limited accountability for military abuses. Ayotzinapa investigations were reported as obstructed, while the National Guard represented continued militarization.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Mostly 2021-2022 evidence and administration-wide context; relevant to 2023 institutional conditions.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes militarization and executive conduct to López Obrador’s administration; abuses involve multiple state actors.","limitations":["Some incidents and statistics precede 2023 and do not establish personal presidential authorization."]},{"source_id":"SRC-aaac1faa31a1f734","start_unit":13,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"Freedom House reported that López Obrador’s administration increased redistributive spending and the minimum wage, but migrant enforcement under National Guard orders generated serious rights abuses; women’s services faced funding cuts and the president dismissed feminists as political opponents. Legal protections for LGBT+ people, workers, and disability rights expanded, while inequality and exploitation persisted.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.7","3B.9","4B.7","5B.1","5B.8","6B.1","6B.3","6B.8","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Administration-wide evidence with several policies and conditions relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes redistributive policy, migration enforcement, women’s-service funding, and presidential rhetoric to López Obrador or his administration.","limitations":["The extract does not quantify 2023 budget execution or service incidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-25ed5331d5f1edd7","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"The supplied page contains only a challenge-validation message and no substantive information about López Obrador, 2023 policy, implementation, or outcomes.","question_ids":[],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"No usable period-specific evidence.","ruler_attribution":"None.","limitations":["The source page is effectively unavailable in the supplied extract."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7479a6325c69c6cc","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"After Category 5 Hurricane Otis struck Acapulco on October 25, 2023, approximately 273,844 homes were affected and 50,000 destroyed, potentially leaving 200,000 people homeless. By November 8, authorities reported 47 deaths, 32 people unaccounted for, 3,821 evacuated, 99 percent power restoration, and a government-led humanitarian and reconstruction response under the armed forces; the government had not appealed for international assistance.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers the October-November 2023 disaster response.","ruler_attribution":"OCHA attributes the response to federal and state authorities, with humanitarian aid under the Mexican Armed Forces; it does not isolate López Obrador’s personal decisions.","limitations":["The report is an early situation snapshot and does not evaluate longer-term recovery, distributional equity, or final outcomes."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-d50873a20cb1f1c1","SRC-e692e02c3ae3a4a0","SRC-79eb7c587c4f45da"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus contains several retrospective reports published after 2023; those facts are included only where they expressly describe 2023 or the López Obrador administration and are labeled with period limitations.","The corpus provides little direct evidence on nuclear risk, arms control, proliferation controls, AI/cyber/biological safeguards, international use of force, fiscal and monetary management, personal financial enrichment, or formal conflict-of-interest compliance.","No scores or chapter-level judgments are provided."]}
